In real accelerator experiments, including at the Large Hadron Collider, a whole stream of particles, consisting of a huge number, collides with a target or with another such stream. Interacting, particles scatter at various angles. The quantity measured in the experiment is the distribution of the number of particles by their scattering angles. Such a distribution is called the scattering cross section. In this problem, we propose you calculate the scattering cross section for a simple case of interaction – elastic collision of rigid bodies. The influence of the gravitational field can be safely neglected throughout the problem.
